notes.md: - **Continent shares (UN WPP 2024):** **Asia** holds about **59%** of world population (2024); **Africa** is second with about **18%**.
- **South Asia ageing:** people aged **65 and above** form about **7.4%** of South Asia's population (2025, World Bank).

new.s: Under Koeppen's classification, which climate type is found in the High Himalaya and Ladakh?
new.x: Koeppen's E type (polar/tundra) covers the High Himalaya and Ladakh.
new.angle: U0643 notes gap: Koeppen E -> High Himalaya, Ladakh

new.s: What is the average annual rainfall of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh gets an average of about 966 mm of rain a year.
new.angle: U0643 notes gap: AP average rainfall 966 mm

new.s: In which month does the coastal belt of Andhra Pradesh receive its peak rainfall?
new.x: The AP coast gets its peak rain in July (south-west monsoon), while Rayalaseema peaks in October-November.
new.angle: U0643 notes gap: AP coast peak rain -> July

new.s: From 2020 onward, the State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCCs) shifted their focus to which of the following?
new.x: SAPCCs moved from mitigation (2010-15) to district-level adaptation from 2020 on.
new.angle: U0643 notes gap: SAPCC shift -> district-level adaptation

new.s: Who among the following first proposed the demographic transition theory in 1929?
new.x: Warren Thompson proposed it in 1929; Frank Notestein named it in 1945.
new.angle: U0644 notes gap: Demographic transition -> Warren Thompson 1929

new.s: According to the optimum population theory, what is the optimum population?
o: The size that gives the highest output per head
The largest population a country can feed
The size at which the birth rate equals the death rate
The size with the lowest population density
new.x: Edwin Cannan's optimum population is the size giving the highest output per head; beyond it there is surplus.
new.angle: U0644 notes gap: Optimum population -> highest output per head

new.s: As per UNFPA's State of World Population 2025, what is India's population?
new.x: SOWP 2025 put India's population at 1.46 billion in 2025.
new.angle: U0644 notes gap: India population 1.46 billion (SOWP 2025)

new.s: According to the UN World Urbanization Prospects 2025, which is the second largest city of the world?
new.x: WUP 2025 ranks Jakarta first, Dhaka second and Tokyo third.
new.angle: U0644 notes gap: WUP 2025 -> Dhaka second largest city

new.s: What was the theme of World Population Day 2026 chosen by India's Ministry of Health and Family Welfare?
o: Healthy Timing and Spacing of Pregnancies
Family Planning is a Human Right
new.x: MoHFW's 2026 theme was Healthy Timing and Spacing of Pregnancies (HTSP).
new.angle: U0644 notes gap: World Population Day 2026 India theme -> HTSP

new.s: What was the world population in 1950?
new.x: The world had about 2.5 billion people in 1950.
new.angle: U0644 notes gap: World population 1950 -> 2.5 billion

new.s: About what share of the world's population lived in Asia in 2024?
new.x: As per UN World Population Prospects 2024 data, Asia holds about 59% of the world's people.
new.angle: U0644 web: #3 continents' shares -> Asia 59%

new.s: Which continent has the second largest share of world population after Asia?
new.x: Africa is second with about 18% of world population (2024), after Asia's about 59%.
new.angle: U0644 web: #3 continents' shares -> Africa second

new.s: In the demographic transition model, Brazil is placed in which stage?
new.x: Brazil is in stage 3 (late expanding): falling birth rate, low death rate.
new.angle: U0645 notes gap: DTM -> Brazil late expanding

new.s: What is the main reason for the highly male-skewed sex ratio of Qatar and the UAE?
new.x: Large inflows of male migrant workers make Qatar and the UAE the most male-skewed countries.
new.angle: U0645 notes gap: Qatar/UAE sex ratio -> male migrant labour

new.s: Which slogan sums up Andhra Pradesh's policy shift from population control to treating children as wealth?
new.x: 'Pillale Sampada' means children are wealth; it marks AP's shift away from population control.
new.angle: U0645 notes gap: AP Pillale Sampada

new.s: As per SRS 2024, which State has the lowest share of elderly population?
new.x: SRS 2024 gives Assam the lowest elderly share (7.6%); Kerala is highest (15%).
new.angle: U0645 notes gap: SRS 2024 lowest elderly share -> Assam

new.s: As per UN World Population Prospects 2022, what is world population projected to be in 2030?
new.x: WPP 2022 projects 8.5 billion by 2030, 9.7 billion by 2050 and 10.4 billion by 2100.
new.angle: U0645 notes gap: WPP 2022 -> 8.5 billion by 2030

new.s: As per World Bank data for 2025, about what share of South Asia's population is aged 65 and above?
new.x: World Bank data put South Asia's 65+ share at about 7.4% in 2025.
new.angle: U0645 web: #5 aged share in South Asia -> about 7.4%

new.s: What was Uttar Pradesh's share of India's population in Census 2011?
new.x: Uttar Pradesh, the most populous State, held 16.49% of India's people in 2011.
new.angle: U0646 notes gap: UP share 16.49%

new.s: Which two new districts were created in Andhra Pradesh's 2025 reorganisation into 28 districts?
new.x: The 2025 reorganisation added Polavaram and Markapuram, taking AP to 28 districts.
new.angle: U0646 notes gap: AP 28 districts -> Polavaram, Markapuram

new.s: What is the area of residual Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Residual AP covers 1,62,970 sq km and ranks 7th by area, ahead of Odisha.
new.angle: U0646 notes gap: Residual AP area 1,62,970 sq km

new.s: Since which Census have the Census Town criteria remained unchanged?
new.x: The Census Town criteria (5,000 people, 400 per sq km, 75% male non-farm workers) are unchanged since 1981.
new.angle: U0646 notes gap: Census Town criteria unchanged since 1981

new.s: Among the southern States, which had the highest population density in Census 2011?
new.x: Kerala had 860 per sq km, ahead of Tamil Nadu (555), Karnataka (319) and undivided AP (308).
new.angle: U0646 notes gap: South India densest -> Kerala 860

new.s: Census 2011 was which census of India after Independence?
new.x: Census 2011 was the 15th census since 1872 and the 7th after Independence.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: Census 2011 -> 7th after Independence

new.s: What was the reference date of Census 2011?
new.x: Census 2011, with the motto 'Our Census, Our Future', had 1 March 2011 as its reference date.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: Census 2011 reference date

new.s: Census 2027 will be the first census of Independent India to do which of the following?
o: Be held under the Census Act, 1948
Count all States at the same time
new.x: Census 2027 is the first caste count in Independent India beyond SC/ST; it is also the first digital census.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: #9 Census 2027 -> first caste count

new.s: On which date was a census with caste enumeration announced for Census 2027?
new.x: The census with caste enumeration was announced on 4 June 2025, to finish by 28 February 2027.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: #14 caste enumeration announced 4 June 2025

new.s: India's population in 2011 roughly equalled the combined population of which group of countries?
o: USA, Indonesia, Brazil, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Japan
USA, Russia, Brazil, Nigeria and Japan
new.x: India's 2011 population was roughly that of the USA, Indonesia, Brazil, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Japan together.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: India 2011 = six countries combined

new.s: What was India's population in Census 1951?
new.x: Census 1951 counted 36.11 crore people; 1971 counted 54.82 crore.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: Census 1951 population 36.11 crore

new.s: What decadal growth of population did Census 1951 record?
new.x: Census 1951 recorded decadal growth of 13.31%; the peak was 24.80% in 1961-71.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: Census 1951 decadal growth 13.31%

new.s: What was India's decadal population growth during 1991-2001?
new.x: Growth was 21.54% in 1991-2001, down from about 24% in 1981-91.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: 1991-2001 decadal growth 21.54%

new.s: By how many percentage points did India's decadal growth fall in 2001-11 compared with 1991-2001?
new.x: Growth fell from 21.54% to 17.7%, a drop of 3.9 points, the sharpest fall since Independence.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: 2001-11 sharpest fall since Independence (3.9 points)

new.s: As per Census 2011, what share of India's population lived in rural areas?
new.x: 68.9% (83.38 crore) were rural and 31.1% urban in 2011.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: Census 2011 rural share 68.9%

new.s:
Arrange the following States in descending order of their 0-6 child population as per Census 2011:
1. Bihar
2. Madhya Pradesh
3. Uttar Pradesh
4. Maharashtra
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
new.x: The largest 0-6 populations were in Uttar Pradesh, then Bihar, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.

new.s: What share of India's population did Scheduled Tribes form in Census 2011?
new.x: STs numbered 10.43 crore, or 8.6% of the population, in 2011.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: ST population 8.6%

new.s: As per Census 2011, which State had the lowest share of elderly population?
new.x: Census 2011 elderly share was lowest in Jharkhand (7.1%) and highest in Kerala (12.6%).
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: Census 2011 lowest elderly share -> Jharkhand

new.s: Which Union Territory recorded the lowest decadal population growth during 2001-11?
new.x: Lakshadweep had the lowest UT growth (6.3%); Dadra and Nagar Haveli the highest (55.9%).
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: #3 lowest-growth UT -> Lakshadweep

new.s: On the old 13-district map, which was the most populous district of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: East Godavari was the largest by population on the 13-district map; SPSR Nellore is on the 28-district map.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: AP largest district (13-district map) -> East Godavari

new.s: What was the annual compound growth rate of India's population during 1891-1921?
new.x: Growth was only about 0.19% a year in 1891-1921, rising to about 2.15% later.
new.angle: U0647 notes gap: Annual growth 1891-1921 -> 0.19%

new.s: According to the Economic Survey 2018-19, what share of India's population would be aged 20-59 at the dividend peak around 2041?
new.x: ES 2018-19 placed the peak around 2041, with 59% of people aged 20-59.
new.angle: U0648 notes gap: ES 2018-19 peak -> 59% aged 20-59

new.s: As per MoHFW projections (March 2026), what will India's 15-59 population be at its peak in 2041?
new.x: MoHFW projects the 15-59 group at 833.8 million (2021), a peak of 1,009.0 million (2041) and 998.1 million (2051).
new.angle: U0648 notes gap: MoHFW 15-59 peak 1,009 million (2041)

new.s: What share of India's population were adolescents (10-19 years) in Census 2011?
new.x: Adolescents aged 10-19 formed 20.9% of India's population in Census 2011.
new.angle: U0648 notes gap: Adolescents 20.9% (Census 2011)

new.s: Which State has a two-child rule for government jobs?
new.x: Assam applies a two-child rule for government jobs.
new.angle: U0648 notes gap: Assam two-child rule

new.s: As per SRS 2024, what is the total fertility rate of urban India?
new.x: SRS 2024 gives India a TFR of 1.9: rural 2.1 and urban 1.5.
new.angle: U0648 notes gap: SRS 2024 urban TFR 1.5

new.s: Mission Parivar Vikas (2016) covers high-fertility districts in how many States?
new.x: It covers 146 districts with TFR 3+ in 7 States: UP, Bihar, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Assam.
new.angle: U0648 notes gap: Mission Parivar Vikas -> 7 States

new.s: What is the median age of Andhra Pradesh's population?
new.x: AP's median age is 32.5 years against India's 28, so AP is ageing faster.
new.angle: U0648 notes gap: AP median age 32.5

new.s: Who described the 'alarming' fall in fertility as 'Shrinconomics' on 1 April 2026?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh's Health Minister used the term 'Shrinconomics' for the fertility fall.
